As of November 2022:
1.1 Review of the Provisional Constitution pending. Sexual Offences Bill and Female Genital Mutilation Bill have been identified as priority legislation on women’s protection by the MoWHRD FGS. 1.2 The 2022 elections resulted in 20% female representation in Parliament, a decrease of 4%. However the election of the 1st Female Deputy Speaker has been recognised as a critical win and milestone for women’s representation at the highest level of government in Somalia. 1.3 Perception study conducted to provide baseline for measurement of perceptions of women in peace processes. 61% of perception survey respondents indicated that they believed women should be in leadership positions for peace processes. 1.1.1 The Somalia National Action Plan on UNSCR 1325 was launched in September 2022 and it will serve as the umbrella framework for all women, peace and security action in Somali including all formal and informal efforts to increase women’s leadership in peace and security processes. 1.1.2 315 (221M, 94F) traditional elders, religious leaders, and women leaders engaged and sensitized across 5 FMS and Banadir Regional Administration. Manual on Women’s Leadership and Participation in Peacebuilding developed 1.1.4 The process to establish and operationalise the Somalia Chapter of the AWLN has been initiated. The interim steering committee of the ALWN will be operationalised in November 2022 and the AWLN launched by the end of December 2022. 1.1.6 Members of the WPP Civil Society Reference Group (CS RG) have been identified through a competitive process. The first convening of the CS RG is scheduled for November 2022. 1.2.1 Roadmap/Advocacy strategy developed on legislative component; Coordination with other stakeholders 1.2.2 Roadmap/Advocacy strategy developed on legislative component; coordination with other stakeholders 1.3.1 National Action Plan on UNSCR 1325 and Somalia Women’s Charter launched in September 2022. Draft Local Action Plans in 5 FMS developed and launch expected in December 2022. 1.3.2 Concept note on Somalia Delivery Exchange on UNSCR 1325 developed and disseminated with stakeholders for review and feedback prior to rollout in 2023. 1.3.3 NAP on UNSCR 1325 Steering Committee established and convened. NAP on UNSCR 1325 Monitoring template developed. Conversations under way on potential to digitise the M&E process for efficiency moving forward. 1.4.1 17 women’s networks established and functional across the 17 target districts; Mapping report on peacemakers, networks and forums commenced. This has created the opportunity for Ministries to engage with the communities across 17 district, which is expected to create ground swell for community leaders and womens groups to be actively involved in legislative and policy formulation. 1.4.2 Capacitation of women’s networks planned for 2023 2.1 Planned for Q1 2023. 2.2 Efforts are ongoing to increase women’s access to justice through new generation UN joint programmes on Justice and Correction. Project launch expected in Q1 2023. 2.3 Interviews and survey of key peacebuilding stakeholders conducted to provide baseline assessment of perceptions of the enabling environment for women’s participation in peacebuilding. Draft assessment received and finalised assessment expected by December 2022 2.1.1 National Action Plan on Conflict Related Sexual Violence adopted in Jan 2022. Policy on human rights finalised by FGS that seeks to strengthen compliance of armed forces with the prohibition against sexual violence in line with international law. Discipline Policy and Code of Conduct developed and implemented by Somalia Police Force. 2.1.2 Three locations for One Stop Centres identified in Kismayo, Baidoa, and Dhusamareb. Centres will be established in 2023. 2.1.3 Datasets not yet available 2.2.1 Religious scholars and networks identified at FGS and FMS levels. Dialogue organized by FGS & FMS Ministries of Women, with participation of Ministry of Religion planned for end November 2022. 2.2.2 Community dialogues planned for 2023. 2.2.3 17 women’s networks have been established across FMS and FGS. In 2023, these networks, as well as other mapped networks and peace platforms, will engage in state and national level engagements on reconciliation 2.3.1 Trainings planned for 2023. 2.3.2 CSOs to implement early-warning mechanisms once capacity building training has taken place. 2.3.3 Engagement will be led by CSOs once capacity building training has taken place. 2.4.1 Media group identified to undertake the media analysis and training through a procurement process. Contract expected to be issued within Q4, 2022. 2.4.2 Planned for 2023 2.4.3 Media group identified to undertake the media analysis and training through a procurement process. Integration of gender components in the Constitutional Review and National Reconciliation Framework and implementation of gender commitments in NDP9

WPP JP provided technical and financial support to develop and launch 2 additional Local Action Plans on UNSCR 1325 in Benadir Region and Galmudug State. Through consistent lobbying and advocacy via various public and high level forums, the Program also contributed to amendment of the Electoral Law that now includes 30 percent quota for women, enactment of anti-FGM Act in Galmudug and adoption of National Strategy to End Violence Against Women and Girls 2024-2029.
